data: Looking for ways to Mo smarter, not harder? You’ve come to the right place. Movember staff members have written this helpful content to guide you through some of the challenges of Movembering.
data.in-this-section#In this section: All the ways you can support Movember How to connect with community Movember is more fun with others

data:
The data is in and there’s no doubt — people who Movember together have more fun and make more impact. The benefits include support, motivation, and collective planning among many others.
There are many ways to connect with others, here are some:
1
data.gather-your-friends#Gather your friends:
You already know people you like to do stuff with — invite your friends to fundraise along with you and support each other’s efforts, and form a team to promote friendly competition and support each other.
Share with them why you do Movember. If it matters to you, chances are it matters to them.
data.join-a-team#Join a team:
Teams are a great way to gather around a common fundraising or Move goal, promote healthy (and fun) competiton, and support each other.
People form teams in all kinds of ways — we have teams of running clubs, workplace colleagues, sports teams, and pub mates.
Start by asking around at work or amnong friends and see if anyone has any teams you could join — they’ll very likely welcome new members.
You can create a team in the Movember App or on movember.com, or search for a team and join that.
2
data.join-an-event#Join an event:
People near you are organising events you can attend. Searching your local area for events is a great way to meet other fundraisers and get tips and support.
Among others you might find Shave Downs, gigs, park runs, and quiz nights.
4
data.join-local-fundraisers#Join local fundra:
There are probably people near you already taking part. Sporting clubs, gyms, community groups, and even networks of mates rally around Movember.
Watch official Movember social media accounts for announcements, or try searching Reddit, Meetup, Facebook groups, or Google.
3

/articles/community/.title: Movember is more fun with others

data:
Starting out with Movember can feel a bit lonely — especially if you’re new, don’t have a big social circle, or aren’t sure how to find other Mo’s. The good news? You’re not alone. Movember is a global movement, and there are plenty of ways to connect with others, build momentum, and feel part of the community.
Here are some easy ways to link up and find your people.
1
data.final-word-youre-never-mo-ing-alone#Fina: Every moustache, every move, every conversation adds to a global movement. Whether you connect online, in your workplace, at an event, or just with one close mate — you’re part of the Mo community. Take the first step, reach out, and you’ll find you’re in good company.
data.find-an-event-near-you#Find an event nea:
From trivia nights to fun runs, Movember events are designed for connection. Don’t worry if you don’t know anyone when you arrive — most people there are looking to connect too.
5
data.join-a-team#Join a team:
Teams are the fastest way to go from solo to connected. Search for a workplace team, sports club, or community group on the Movember site. Or start your own team and invite a few friends — even a team of two feels better than one.
3
data.jump-into-online-movember-spaces#Jump in:
Not everyone has local Mo’s to link up with, but the internet’s always open, as is the Movember app. Join online communities and Movember social channels where you can swap tips, share progress, and cheer on other fundraisers.
4
data.lean-into-movembers-bigger-story#Lean in: If you feel awkward asking, remember: you’re not fundraising for yourself, you’re part of a global mission to change the face of men’s health. Sharing the bigger picture makes it easier to talk to strangers, neighbours, or co-workers.
data.link-up-at-work-or-school#Link up at wor:
If you’re new, you might be surprised who else is quietly Mo-ing. Put a shoutout in Slack, Teams, or a group email: “Anyone doing Movember this year?” Chances are, you’ll find instant teammates and allies.
6
data.start-small-and-share-your-story#Start s:
Even if your network feels tiny, start with what you’ve got. Post on social media, drop your Mo Space link in a group chat, or tell a mate over coffee. People often surprise you — someone you don’t expect might be your first donor or even join your fundraiser.
Sharing your story might just be the best way to drive interactions online — explain your personal connection to the Movember cause. Also consider recording a video of you speaking to maximise the engagement.
2
data.support-others-even-if-you-dont-know-the:
Leave comments on Mo Spaces, donate a few bucks to another fundraiser, or share someone else’s story. It’s a quick way to feel connected, and often they’ll return the favour.
7

data:
There’s more than one way to Mo! Here is your list of ways you can contribute to Movember beyond fundraising.
1
data.attend-local-events#Attend local events:
Check out what’s happening near you – trivia nights, barbecues, fun runs, and community gatherings are all part of the Movember magic. Show up, bring friends, donate if you can, and spread the word.
9
data.be-a-corporate-matchmaker#Be a corporate:
Encourage your employer to match staff donations, or get the workplace to host a Movember day (think moustache dress-ups, Movember lunches, or a team Move challenge).
10
data.be-a-mo-mentor#Be a Mo Mentor:
If you’ve done Movember before, guide a first-timer: help them set goals, promote their Mo Space, and keep spirits high.
11
data.donate#Donate:
If you’re not up for running a fundraiser yourself, you can still make a huge difference by donating to a mate’s Mo Space or directly to Movember. Every contribution fuels lifesaving programs in mental health, suicide prevention, prostate cancer, and testicular cancer.
3
data.raise-awareness#Raise awareness:
Share the Movember message, or share your story. There are almost unlimited ways to do this. Some of our favourites:
Share one of our pre-made messages to social media, or roll your own. Get on your workplace or school Slack, Teams, or group email and share what Movember is all about. Repost Movember content from social media. Share a personal story about why you support men’s health – authenticity inspires action. Add a Movember banner to your email signature, website, or storefront to spark curiosity and conversations. 5
data.raise-funds-your-way#Raise funds your wa:
Grow, Move and Host are very popular and the sky’s the limit when you Mo Your Own Way. Host a quiz night, bake sale, or Mo-lympics challenge. Get creative and use your talents to bring people together while raising dollars for men’s health. Every little thing you do counts.
2
data.start-a-conversation#Start a conversatio:
Chances are you are here because you care about men’s health, so why not chat to others on this important subject? Ask a mate how they’re really going. Check in regularly. Small, honest conversations can literally save lives.
Conversations are most effective in-person but also matter when you go online. Start a thread, reply with encouragement, or share your experience.
Some useful links:
Movember conversation starters How to have a conversation with a man who is struggling 6
data.support-others#Support others:
Not everyone can fundraise, but everyone can support. Volunteer at a Movember event, help a mate with their fundraiser, or offer your skills (design, baking, logistics, whatever!) to make their efforts go further.
8
data.support-year-round#Support year-round:
Men’s health doesn’t stop on November 30. Keep the conversation alive, volunteer with men’s health groups, or check in with mates regularly.
However you Mo, you’re part of the movement.
data.wear-movember-merch#Wear Movember merch:
Rep the cause with pride. Grab a Movember tee, cap, or hoodie from the Movember store and become a walking, talking awareness machine. Bonus: merch sales also support men’s health projects.
Official merch storemovember.store 4
data.write-supporting-messages-to-other-fundr:
Show some love to your fellow Mo’s. Jump on their Mo Space and leave a comment, cheer them on, or thank them for what they’re doing. Fundraising is easier (and more fun) when people feel supported.
7

/articles/supporting/.title: All the ways you can support Movember

data: Fundraising fuels the mission. Whether you’re flying solo, teaming up, or rallying the workplace, this is your playbook. From asking for donations to smashing it on social, we’ve got the tools to help you go big, have fun, and change the face of men’s health.
data.in-this-section#In this section: Fundraising resources Fundraising in teams Promoting your fundraiser Social media assets Workplace fundraising Facebook fundraisers Asking for donations Platinum Club Keeping it legal Getting support

data:
To help you live your best Mo, here are some donation ideas from our fundraising experts in the Mo community.
Family and friends first - They’ll be the most supportive. Especially if you have embarrassing photos of them.
Back yourself - Make the first donation and challenge others to match it.
Tried and true - Ask those who’ve supported you in the past. You’ll find their email details in your online Mo Space. Go to your ‘My account’ section, then click on ‘Fundraising history’. Share why you’re doing it! If you have a reason or personal story you want to share, tell it. We’re all here to inspire conversations and change the face of men’s health.
data.ask-again#Ask again: Once more for the people in the back! Remind everyone that you’re doing Movember and why it’s important to you. Include your Mo Space web link (the URL) and/or QR code to make donating as easy as possible. Sometimes people just need a reminder, so don’t be afraid to repeat yourself.
data.for-mens-health#For men’s health:
Let them know why men’s health needs them.
“Globally, we lose a man to suicide every minute.” “Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in men.” “Testicular cancer is the #1 cancer in young men.” “Our fathers, partners, brothers and friends are dying before their time.”
data.offline-donations#Offline donations: Loads of donors will send money straight to your Mo Space; but for those who give you cash, cheques or bank transfers, use the ‘Submit cash donations’ section on your Mo Space to send the donations directly to Movember.
data.pre-written-emails-and-social-posts#Pre-:
We know – not everyone’s a wordsmith. Most of us would rather be out and about sweating for Movember instead of sweating in front of a blank Word doc. Our scribes have written some email templates for you to send out and really get donations flowing. Download the templates from our fundraising resources page.
And rest safe in the knowledge, every single donation you get, whether it’s 1 or 1000, will help to change the face of men’s health. And that my friend, is something very special.
data.progress-updates#Progress updates: Photos, updates and Mo musings – keep your donors (and potential donors) in the loop.
data.tips-on-asking-for-donations#Tips on ask: Since we’re veterans at asking for donations, we’ve added a slew of template messages to your Mo Space that you can use. Don’t just take our words, though; add a personal touch as you send messages via email, social media, or even offline with individual thank you cards – something they’ll really remember.
data.update-your-target#Update your target: If you smash your target with time to spare, why not up the ante? Inspire more donations by increasing your target.

data:
Here you’ll find some helpful tips and legal guidance on how to use our branding to best support us.
Movember’s branding consists of several globally registered trademarks including the word Movember and our brand expression ‘changing the face of men’s health’.
Our iconic mo and Movember logos are protected, as is the imagery and artwork used on the Movember website.
data.cause-related-marketing#Cause-related ma:
Cause-related marketing is offering products for sale on the basis that a % or amount per sale will be donated to Movember.
As a registered charity, Movember has a range of regulatory obligations for these sorts of arrangements (e.g. we need to have a written agreement with the seller of the product and complete certain regulatory filings) so we only do a small number each year.
If you would like to explore this further with us then please get in touch by email at info@movember.com and we can send you more information.
data.do#Do: Do use the downloadable artwork on our website to promote your participation in Movember (see movember.com/support-us/fundraising-resources). E.g. Use the campaign logos in a Facebook post or tweet about growing your Mo (but don’t alter or manipulate the downloaded images). Do give your event a distinctive name and state that it is in support of Movember. E.g. ‘Community Ball supporting Movember’. Do give your website, app or product a unique name. Do mention and link to Movember and promote your involvement with our cause. Do sign up at movember.com or via the Movember app and start a team for your company and your staff.
data.dont#Don’t: Don’t sell items that display our branding(including the word MOVEMBER or our iconic mo). This includes clothing, accessories, products or any merchandise created for sale, unless you have a written agreement with Movember (see Cause-related marketing section). Don’t call your event an “Official” Movember event**. This can confuse the community about who is organising and responsible for the event. E.g. Don’t call your event the “Official Movember Gala”. Don’t use the word MOVEMBER, or anything confusingly similar in the name of your website or a social media account, business name, app or product. E.g. Don’t call your app “Movember Moustache” or name your business “Movember Org.” Don’t offer goods or services for sale on the basis that a % or number of dollars per sale will be donated to Movember, unless you have a written agreement with Movember (see Cause-related marketing section).
data.insurance#Insurance:
Sometimes if you are organising an event at a venue or public space (e.g. for a Move event), the venue owner or local government will ask you to provide proof of insurance.
Members of the Movember community sometimes ask us if they can use our public liability insurance for these purposes. Unfortunately, Movember’s insurance policies only cover events organised by Movember and we cannot extend our coverage for third-party events.
data.liquor-licensing#Liquor licensing:
Sometimes if you are organising an event, the venue owner or event supplier will ask to use Movembers’ charitable registration number to receive a liquor permit or licence.
Unfortunately, for liability and tax reasons, Movember cannot allow the use of its charitable registration number for non-official Movember events.
For more information on the rules surrounding third-party events organised to support Movember, please contact info@movember.com.
data.other#Other:
Please don’t engage in the following types of fundraising on behalf of Movember:
Telemarketing Door to door fundraising Collecting money in public places, such as at intersections
data.other-fundraising-activities#Other fundr:
If you want to hold a specific fundraising event or activity then we can support you by:
Providing downloadable assets. Check out the available gear on our website. Listing the details of the event on the Movember website. Check out the local Movember events in your community. Connecting you with a Movember community engagement leader to help you get your event off the ground – contact info@movember.com. You are responsible for organising your event. Some of the things you might need to take care of are:
All financial aspects of your fundraising event, including ensuring that funds donated to Movember at the event are remitted to Movember following the event (for information about issuing receipts, see movember.com/faq). Local government permits. Any required activity permits for competitions. Food handling permits. Security services. Health and safety/fire plans. In addition, you will be responsible for the insurance and liquor licensing requirements for your event.

data:
What if we told you that you’re likely to raise 180% more funds than your average Mo by using one simple trick? With Facebook Fundraisers, you can easily link your Mo Space fundraiser profile and Facebook account. That way, friends and family can donate to your Movember fundraiser directly through Facebook – they don’t even need to leave the app.
Donations sync both ways. That means all donations received through Facebook appear on your Mo Space; and all direct donations to your Mo Space contribute to your Facebook fundraising goal. Pretty neat, right? And it’s all done with a few simple steps.
Create a Mo Space page FIRST – it has to be created before you do anything else! Head to your Mo Space and look for the Facebook icon (don’t go to Facebook, if you create it from Facebook we can’t link it) Click to create your Facebook Fundraiser You’ll need to sign into your Facebook account and follow the prompts Once finished, you’ll be dropped back on your Mo Space where you can click ‘View your Facebook Fundraiser’ Post a pic to your Facebook Fundraiser or kick off by donating to yourself, then sit back and watch the donations roll in Visit your Mo Space to set up your Facebook Fundraiser now. (You can also do a fundraiser for Movember on Instagram but sadly we don’t have the power (yet) to connect that to your Mo Space – so it won’t contribute to your total).
data.having-trouble#Having trouble?: Get in touch with your local Mo Team.

data:
Being a “legend” gets bandied around a bit these days. But our research shows it’s something that all Mo’s/Mo supporters around the world have in common.
So how does a legend become a rockstar? It’s not easy, but those that fundraise $1500 or more in a year will join the Movember Platinum Club and receive “rockstar status”.
Our rockstars also gain exclusive access to:
Platinum Club badges and photo stickers on your Mo Space and App. Invitations to exclusive Movember Community events. Opportunity to purchase Platinum Club Merch. News, updates, toolkits and resources to share with your community and help spread the word about men’s health. To find out more on Movember’s Platinum Club visit movember.com.

As a part of the Mo Community, your job is to shout about it, tell your story, share your page, tell everyone what you’re doing. Your friends, your parents, people down the shops, at the barbers, at work, in the gym, at footy, ANYWHERE you can tell people about Movember. It’s what we Mo’s do. And if you’re not doing it in person, there are lots of other ways to share.
data.email#Email: We’ve got some excellent pre-written messages you can use to hit up your address book for donations. Get in touch with your network the not-quite-old-fashioned way.
data.local-press#Local press: If you’re doing something really out there to Mo Your Own Way, or taking on a huge physical challenge, or sporting a rainbow moustache for the whole month, we’re pretty sure your local media outlet would love to hear about it. Think about how many people you could reach with your Mo message! Check out your local paper or radio website for details on sharing your story.
data.social-media#Social media:
Facebook/Instagram/Twitter/TikTok/BeReal/whatever the new thing is.
Tell people what you’re doing and why. You could livestream your shave down, if you’re running every day, upload a photo each time with an update on how your legs are feeling. If you have a personal reason for supporting Movember, and feel comfortable sharing, tell people. You could help someone going through something similar, inspire another Mo to join the community, or get a few more donations. Repetition is key – not everyone is on social media every day, and sometimes people mean to donate but forget. Don’t let them miss what you’re doing or forget. You’ve got 30 wonderful days to share that Mo joy. Photos/videos - let everyone see that beautiful face - Mo or not. Or where you’re running today. Or the behind the scenes of you setting up your big Mo bash.
data.the-movember-app#The Movember app:
You can share your Mo Space directly from movember.com or from the app. Here are three fancy features that’ll make you an irresistible donation magnet:
Mo Selfie: the camera is loaded with custom stickers and filters to spice up your Mo Mo Space: speedy access to your Mo Space means easier everything. Asking for and receiving donations, thanking donors, and sharing your page. Mo Tracker: the Mo Tracker measures daily Mo growth and then pulls it all together in an end-of-month timelapse.
data.whatsapptext#WhatsApp/Text: Use our templates to get the word out on the whatsapp groups, whether it’s your mates, your neighbours or a work group – all good groups of people who’ll be interested to hear why you’re fundraising for Movember this year.

You’ll have fun, build connections and strengthen camaraderie with friends, peers and colleagues. Your teammates keep you fired up. You dial the competitive up to 11. A team makes a bigger impact — and that means more much-needed funds and awareness for men’s health.
Every team has a page that shows the Team Captain, fundraising target, and donation tally. You can also check out the feed to see donations, messages and photos from the team.
data.captains#Captains:
Team Captains are legendary Movember supporters. Change agents. Chief motivators. Champion recruiters. You lead by example, inspiring and motivating others to shake things up and get behind the cause.
You’ll recruit and build a team and together with your teammates, you’ll raise funds and awareness to help change the face of men’s health.
Download the Captain’s Toolkit
data.fundraising-as-a-team#Fundraising as a t:
The best way to raise funds is to build a strong team, inspire them to get involved, and have fun while you’re at it. Get creative – the sky’s the limit.
Team fundraising ideas:
Host a Movember kick-off party on Movember 1st with an office Shave Down, morning coffee, themed lunch or go for a team run to kick off your Move. Set a fundraising and/or Move target with your team, and make a plan to crush it. Ask for donations through email and social media, with a link to your team’s Mo Space. Personalise your Mo Space with pictures, videos, updates and team members’ personal stories. Add the team’s Mo Space URL to your email signature. Use your Mo Space leaderboards to compete with and motivate each other. Get your biz to back the Mo by sharing Movember’s health messages and stories through internal communication channels. And don’t forget to ask your employer if they’ll match your team’s fundraising efforts. Sacrifice your existing facial hair (beards, goatees etc.) for donations. Leave a donation box in your break room, locker room or wherever you gather regularly. Give weekly prizes for the best Mo, Mover and fundraiser. Auction off the Mo you’ll Grow (meaning others get to make the call on the style of Mo you Grow). Get senior members of your organisation on board (we can help with this). Throw an end-of-month awards ceremony to toast the top fundraiser, Mover and, of course, the best and worst Mo’s. Make sure the donation box moves around the room. Encourage your team mates to download the app to enhance their Movember experience. Start some banter in the group chat, share your Mogress and get wild with our range of Mo-filters.
data.join-a-team#Join a team: To join a team, head to the team section of your Mo Space online, or to the ‘Team’ tab of the Movember App. Search for an existing team and ask to join.
data.starting-a-team#Starting a Team:
To start a team, head to the team section of your Mo Space, or to the ‘Team’ tab of the Movember App. Starting a team makes you the default Team Captain — every team needs one. A legendary Movember supporter. Chief motivator. Champion recruiter. One who leads by example.
Choose a team name — Your first responsibility is a team name. Beardless Dragons? The Hairy Marys? Choose wisely. A good name makes recruiting team members easier. The bigger your crew, the bigger your impact.
Set a fundraising target — Set a fundraising target with your team and make a plan to blow past expectations.
Define the team’s motivation — Like a personal Mo Space, make it meaningful.
Personalize your Mo Space — Give your Mo Space a personal touch with pictures, videos, plenty of updates, and team members’ personal stories.
Keep the feed active — Activate the team feed with some accolades. Shout out to the person with the best 5 o’clock shadow or who’s moved the most on day one.
Build your team — The mo the merrier. Share your team’s Mo Space QR code and encourage your friends, colleagues, and community to join in the fun.

data: Ready to kick things off? This is where you’ll find the essentials — from picking your way to Mo, to setting up your Mo Space, to getting the app that keeps it all moving. Dive in and start strong.

data: Whether you’re taking on Movember’s Move challenge or Mo Your Own Way, linking your fitness app lets you track your progress and share updates that inspire donations. All while motivating you to smash your target.
data.keep-in-mind#Keep in mind: Movember only records sessions you start and stop tracking using the activities you’ve selected. We won’t track any additional distance covered outside of these prompts. It can take a while for your tracked activity to appear on your Mo Space. Don’t worry if you can’t see it immediately – it’s coming. Your Mo Space will only display your completed sessions after you’ve connected your fitness app. Your activity will only sync if the activity type used on your device/app matches one of those you picked as your Move/MYOW challenge. For example; if you select run on mo.com, but log a cycle that won’t push over.
data.privacy-and-troubleshooting#Privacy and:
Your privacy matters — To read about the information that your fitness app shares with Movember, visit movember.com/privacy.
Having trouble? — If you can’t sync your fitness app to your Mo Space, get in touch with your local Mo Team.
data.three-simple-steps#Three simple steps: Fire up the Movember app or log into your Mo Space on movember.com. Set your Move challenge by selecting ‘Run’, ‘Walk’, ‘Cycling’, ‘Swimming’, or ‘Rowing’. Follow the prompts to connect your fitness app. The Movember app supports Garmin Connect, Fitbit, and Strava. Movember.com supports Garmin Connect, Fitbit and Strava.

How to join a Movember Challenge: Sign up for Movember and create a Movember team, online or in the app. Rally your friends/co-workers/family to sign up, too.

data:
With fundraising, just like in physics, breaking inertia and building momentum is hard. But also small actions can amount to a big bang. Here are our top tips for newbies and Mo-Pros alike to get a Movember fundraiser gathering momentum like a trout off a waterfall.
1
data.ask-a-friend-or-family-member-to-donate-:
Friends and family are your biggest fans and are often the most likely to contribute. A donation from them helps build momentum and encourages others to give. Ask them to spread the word that you are doing Movember this year and hopefully gather more donations.
5
data.bring-your-workplace-on-board#Bring your:
See if your workplace will support you – whether that’s a dollar-for-dollar match, a bake sale in the lunchroom, or the boss shaving their head if you hit your target. Office banter + moustaches = fundraising gold.
8
data.donate-to-yourself#Donate to yourself:
It shows you’re committed and breaks the dreaded ‘$0 raised’ (or 0 Euro, 0 Pesos, or 0 Galactic Credits) barrier, making it easier for others to follow your lead.
4
data.dont-overthink-it#Don’t overthink it:
Here’s the thing about fundraising – don’t overcomplicate it. The lamest moustaches historically raise the most money, so don’t stress about looking as good as Tom Selleck. Just sign up for whatever makes sense to you, just get started.
Whether you Grow, Move, Host or Mo your own way there is a way to a fundraise for everyone. Choose what is going to be enjoyable for you. Fun is what keeps the Mo on the go.
2
data.keep-it-fun#Keep it fun: Wear a silly costume, add quirky challenges, or promise to dye your moustache a ridiculous colour when you hit your target. Fundraising is contagious when it looks like fun.
data.promote-your-fundraiser#Promote your fun:
Don’t keep your fundraiser a secret. Share updates on social media, drop your Mo Space link into WhatsApp or Slack groups, and don’t be afraid to ask more than once. People are busy, and often just need a reminder. The more you share your story, the more support you’ll attract.
6
data.rally-supporters#Rally supporters:
The magic happens when people connect and combine efforts. Ask friends, collegues, team mates, or other students “What are you doing for Movember?” You’ll be surprised how many people want to collaborate.
7
data.set-goals-and-make-a-plan#Set goals, and:
Fundraising is easier when you know what you’re aiming for. Pick a realistic fundraising goal or keep it low for now and update it when you hit the goal.
Then make a simple plan for how you’ll get there. Share your goal publicly so people can help you smash it. And don’t be shy – stretch goals can keep momentum rolling once you’ve hit the first milestone.
3

data:
Growing a Mo is the most well known way of supporting Movember.
But you don’t need to grow to save a bro. Move, Host and Mo Your Own Way are options which may better suit your calling. You can even chop, change and combine as you please.
data.grow#Grow:
Grow a moustache to raise funds for men’s health. It’s the classic and simple approach. Can’t grow one? Even better. The worse the Mo, the more conversations it’ll inspire. It’s how you can literally get in the movement.
How to Grow
data.host#Host:
Rally a crew and host a trivia night or a ping-pong tournament. Anything close to you or your community’s heart can inspire an event.
How to Host
data.mo-your-own-way#Mo Your Own Way:
A choose-your-own-adventure challenge epic in scope and scale. Set your sights on breaking an obscure record. Do dares for donations. Kick a bad habit. Take on a physical challenge. Mo Your Own Way means you make the rules.
How to Mo Your Own Way
data.move#Move:
Move this Movember by walking or running 60km over the month. That’s 60km for the 60 men we lose to suicide each hour globally. Solo and team efforts accepted.
How to Move

data: The place where it all started – growing a moustache on our top lip to raise funds for men’s health That means growing a Mo for the month formerly known as November. And it starts by making sure you’re clean shaven using a Gillette razor on the first day of Movember.
data.dye-it#Dye it:
Nothing gets more attention than a pink or purple Mo. Want to raise more? Offer to dye it in colours you hate for extra dough.
4
data.mo-sweepstake#Mo sweepstake:
Auction off the style of your Mo for donations – either to the highest bidder or in a raffle.
5
data.shave-down#Shave-down:
There’s no better way to kick start your fundraising than to share the evidence of you shaving down on the 1st Movember. Not only will you be ready to start Movember fresh faced and itching to get going, you can also use this as a chance to get the donations rolling in. Live stream, video or get your mates together and shave down in person.
2
data.show-your-mo-gress#Show your mo-gress:
Use the Movember app to take a daily photo and share your Mo-gress using our built in GIF creator. Create and share videos and use our filters to splash your ‘tache all over your social media.
3
data.the-keeper#The Keeper: Not everyone’s a Mo fan. So, what happens if you announce that you plan to keep yours? Maybe it’s an opportunity to get donations to shave it off. Just sayin’.

data: Rally your crew and Host a Mo-ment to raise awareness and funds for men’s health. You can Host in person or online – think big and go wild. It’s all about having a good time and raising funds for a good cause.
data.bing-mo#Bing-Mo: Host a bingo night and ask players to donate for their bingo cards. There’s a number of websites out there that generate cards for free, and even randomly select the numbers for you to call.
data.mo-trivia#Mo Trivia:
Think classic pub trivia with a bonus Mo themed round. Put people in teams for some friendly competition. Offer prizes, ask for donations to enter.
3
data.shave-down#Shave Down:
Get the gang together on Movember 1st for a Shave Down. Have a barber on hand to bring out those baby faces.
2
data.sports-tournament#Sports Tournament:
Decide on your sport, time and date and find a suitable venue. Promote it far and wide to get teams signed up – it’s a good idea to ask for them to pay to secure their space so they are committed to attending. As well as raising funds through the entry fees you can also have extra fundraising activities on the day, like a silent auction or sweepstake.
5
data.throw-a-stache-bash#Throw a Stache Bash:
Invite your friends, family and supporters to an end-of-Movember party. Ask for donations as an entry fee, set up some fun activities and thank everyone for helping you change the face of men’s health.
4

data: Run or walk 60km/mi over the month. That’s 60km/mi for the 60 men we lose to suicide each hour, every hour across the world. Movember isn’t just about growing a furry top lip – it’s also about changing men’s health by getting a sweat on for the month of Movember.
data.friendly-competition#Friendly competitio:
Throw down a challenge to your friends: who will be first to complete their 60km? The winner receives a donation to their Mo Space.
3
data.move-for-the-masses#Move for the masses:
Gather your friends or colleagues for a group run. Recruit someone to be the leader of the pack, then ready, set, sweat!
2
data.move-in-twos#Move in twos:
Get a friend on board and walk your 60km together. If for whatever reason you can’t do it in person, plug in your earphones and give each other a call. It’s also a great opportunity to check in with each other.
4
data.move-multiplier#Move multiplier:
Ask your network to pledge a donation amount for every km that you move.
If you can get five people to pledge $1 per km, that’s $300 raised.
5
data.track-your-move#Track your move: Attach your fitness tracker. Track your Move progress by attaching your fitness tracker to your MoSpace. For all relevant details head to page 15.

data: Mo Your Own Way means you make the rules – choose an activity that pushes you out of your comfort zone. Set your sights on breaking a world record. Do dares for donations. Kick a bad habit. Take on a physical challenge. Think big and go bigger.
data.dares-for-donations#Dares for Donations:
They set the dare and name their donation amount. You go all out for men’s health (as long as it’s safe and legal of course). Check out some awesome ideas to get you going.
4
data.have-fun-doin-good#Have fun, doin’ good: Whatever you do, however much you raise, if you’re having a good time, you’re nailing it.
data.miles-for-mens-health#Miles for Men’s He:
Rally a group and set your sights on the horizon – each person runs a leg to hit a combined target, like the distance from one capital city to the next. Pull together to inspire donations.
3
data.mo-without#Mo Without:
Get sponsored to give up caffeine, sugar or alcohol for the month. Fine yourself when you fumble. You’ll raise funds and improve your health. Win, win.
5
data.raise-some-brows#Raise some brows: The best challenges tend to prompt the response “you’re doing what?!” Get that right and donations will follow.
data.take-a-hike#Take a Hike:
From a one-day trek to a multi-day challenge, scale mountains and watch your donations soar.
2
data.use-your-talents#Use Your Talents: Are you a marvellous musician, a fantastic photographer or a star baker? Harness your skills for donations from friends, family and colleagues.
data.whenever-wherever#Whenever, wherever: Indoors, outdoors, in a single day, over several weeks or across the year. This is your challenge. You make the rules.
